newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong govt sees 22,000 flats completed in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong govt sees 22,000 flats completed in 1997.

text.p: Almost 20,000 flats were built in Hong Kong last year, with more than 70 percent of them in the New Territories, the government said on Friday.
The Rating and Valuation Department said in a statement the number of units forecast for completion in 1997 would rise to some 22,000.
Taken together with the units vacant at the end of 1996, would mean availability of around 56,000 units for occupation this year, it said.
In 1998, completions of units were expected to increase to about 36,000 including smaller projects, the department said
Prices of flats in selected popular developments at year end were up 31 percent from December 1995 but only marginally above the April 1994 peak, it said.
The territory-wide price index for the last quarter showed an overall increase of 23 percent over a year earlier but the rental index showed a much lower four percent, it said.

Completions of Grade A offices in 1996 were 131,000 square metres, about eight percent higher than that forecast a year earlier but 52 percent below the five-year average of 272,000 square metres between 1991 and 1995.
Vacant space amounted to about 354,000 square metres, representing 8.3 percent of stock.
The forecast for Grade A office completions was at 344,000 square metres in 1997 and 500,000 in 1998, it said.
